deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT (from p.44): Hilbert is building diagonal-type Padé approximants of the binomial function (1-z)^alpha. He takes polynomials N(z) and Z(z) with f(z) = N(z)(1-z)^alpha - Z(z) = z^{2n}(1 + ...). The z^{2n} normalisation is from p.44. The degrees deg N = n and deg Z = n-1 are my inference; they are the only choice consistent with the 2n-1 coefficient conditions and with the Fuchs relation below. Via the Wronskian G = Z'N - ZN' + ..., he showed on p.44 that the ODE satisfied by f has singularities only at 0, 1 and infinity, all of Riemann (Fuchsian) type.

THIS PAGE.

(a) The singular points. The functions f, N(1-z)^alpha and Z all solve the same second-order linear ODE. The reason given: going around z=1, (1-z)^alpha changes only by a constant factor. Only two of the three are independent, since f = N(1-z)^alpha - Z. From their local behaviour one reads off the characteristic exponents:
- at z=0: {0, 2n} (from Z and f);
- at z=1: {0, alpha} (from Z and N(1-z)^alpha);
- at z=infinity: {1-n, -n-alpha} (from Z ~ z^{n-1} and N(1-z)^alpha ~ z^{n+alpha}).
[Mine] The Fuchs relation checks: 0 + 2n + 0 + alpha + (1-n) + (-n-alpha) = 1.

(b) The ODE. 'Hierdurch erhält man die folgende Differentialgleichung' refers to the Riemann P-symbol P{0: 0, 2n; 1: 0, alpha; inf: 1-n, -n-alpha}. [Mine] Pulling out z^{2n} gives f = c * z^{2n} * 2F1(n+1, n-alpha; 2n+1; z), i.e. the Gauss hypergeometric equation. Hilbert does not write it out; he refers to his own exercises on linear ODEs ('am Schluss').

(c) The continued fraction. He remarks that for the continued fraction one needs nothing beyond the partial numerators (m±alpha)/(2(2m-1)). [Mine] These are the Gauss continued-fraction coefficients for F(-alpha,1;1;z) = (1-z)^alpha:
(1-z)^alpha = 1/(1 + alpha z/(1 - k2 z/(1 - k3 z/(1 - ...)))),
with k_{2m} = (m+alpha)/(2(2m-1)) and k_{2m+1} = (m-alpha)/(2(2m+1)).

(d) Convergence by Riemann's method. Let P_n/Q_n be the even convergent (n=2m), with f_n = Q_n(1-z)^alpha - P_n.
- Analytic continuation around z=1 gives (f_n) = Q_n(1-z)^alpha e^{2 pi i alpha} - P_n.
- Hence f_n - (f_n) = Q_n(1-z)^alpha(1 - e^{2 pi i alpha}).
- [Mine] So the relative error (1-z)^alpha - P_n/Q_n = f_n/Q_n = (1-z)^alpha(1 - e^{2 pi i alpha}) * f_n/(f_n - (f_n)).
- Convergence therefore reduces to lim f_n/(f_n - (f_n)) = 0. This is equivalent to lim f_n/(f_n) = 0, since r/(r-1) -> 0 iff r -> 0.
This comparison of the two branches of a hypergeometric solution with growing parameters is Riemann's method from his posthumous fragment on continued fractions of hypergeometric quotients. Hilbert cites the fragment, Thomé (Crelle 66, 67) and Heine, Kugelfunctionen I p.270. The page does not carry out the asymptotic estimate itself.

(e) Marginal research programme (top of page). Approximate (1+x)^{sqrt2} and (1+x)^{-sqrt2} simultaneously by two rational fractions with a common denominator. Do this via a special (multidimensional, Jacobi-Perron/Hermite-Padé type II) continued-fraction algorithm, and so prove e.g. that 2^{sqrt2} is irrational (x=1). The next page extends the plan to 'dreifache Kettenalgorithmen' for 2F1 and Bessel functions.
errors: The factor list (m±alpha)/(2(2m-1)) is imprecise: in Gauss's continued fraction for (1-z)^alpha the '+' coefficients are (m+alpha)/(2(2m-1)), but the '-' coefficients are (m-alpha)/(2(2m+1)). Probably shorthand or a slip.
The convergence argument is only reduced to lim f_n/(f_n)=0. The needed asymptotics of the two hypergeometric branches are not given; they are deferred to Riemann, Thomé and Heine.

The plan to prove 2^{sqrt2} irrational via Hermite-Padé approximation of (1+x)^{±sqrt2} has a flaw not addressed here. The approximating polynomials have coefficients in Q(sqrt2) with denominators like k! (binom(sqrt2,k)), not geometric ones. So the usual integrality/size argument used for rational exponents does not go through. The problem was settled only by Gelfond/Kuzmin (1929-30) and Gelfond-Schneider (1934) with different methods.

Line 'die Wurzeln der charakteristischen Gleichungen...' is a sentence fragment continuing from p.44 ('bestimme aus den Entwickelungsanfängen der 3 Functionen ... die Wurzeln'). Not an error, but grammatically incomplete in isolation.

results.what: Padé approximants of (1-z)^alpha: the remainder z^{2n}(...) satisfies a hypergeometric (Riemann P) equation with exponents {0,2n},{0,alpha},{1-n,-n-alpha}
results.modern_name: Padé approximants to the binomial function / hypergeometric representation of the Padé remainder

results.what: Gauss continued fraction for (1-z)^alpha with partial numerators (m+alpha)/(2(2m-1)), (m-alpha)/(2(2m+1))
results.modern_name: Gauss continued fraction for 2F1(a,1;c;z) specialised to the binomial

results.what: Convergence proof by comparing the remainder f_n with its analytic continuation around z=1: error ∝ f_n/(f_n-(f_n))
results.modern_name: Riemann's method for convergence of hypergeometric continued fractions (monodromy/branch comparison)

results.what: Programme: simultaneous rational approximation of (1+x)^{sqrt2}, (1+x)^{-sqrt2} with common denominator by a generalized continued-fraction algorithm, to prove irrationality of 2^{sqrt2}
results.modern_name: Hermite-Padé (type II / simultaneous) approximation as an irrationality method; Hilbert's 7th problem
results.usually_credited_to: Hermite (1873) for the method; 2^{sqrt2} transcendence: Gelfond, Kuzmin (1929-30), Gelfond-Schneider (1934); Siegel (1929) for systematic Hermite-Padé use

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics actually carried out is classical: Padé/Gauss continued fraction for (1-z)^alpha and Riemann's convergence method. The interesting item is the research note. It shows that, probably in the 1890s, Hilbert planned to attack the irrationality of 2^{sqrt2} (later his 7th problem) via simultaneous Hermite-Padé approximation of (1+x)^{±sqrt2}. The next page extends this to Bessel and hypergeometric functions, anticipating Siegel-style ideas. Hilbert's interest in 2^{sqrt2} is well known, though. The plan is only a sketch and would not work as stated, so this is a notable unpublished detail rather than a major result.

transcription_corrections: First line: probably 'Nähere (1+x)^{√2} und (1+x)^{-√2} simultan durch 2 rationale Brüche mit demselben Nenner an durch einen besonderen Kettenbruch-Algorithmus'. The leading 'x' before (1+x)^{√2} appears to be struck or overwritten.
'aus Schlurr[?]' should read 'am Schluss' (i.e. 'Meine Uebungen zur Theorie der linearen Differentialgl. am Schluss').
In the reference line 'ferner' is an interlinear insertion before the struck 'Heine' and 'Thomé'; the struck 'S. 270' follows Thomé, and the final reference is 'Heine Kugelfunctionen I S. 270'.
The partial numerators are written m±α over 2(2m-1), as transcribed. Mathematically, the minus case should have 2(2m+1).
